title: 第一卷 第2章 吃上肉
novel_title: 津门武圣，从苦力开始每日结算
content_zh:
雨停了。

    空气里依旧是那股子挥之不去的腥味，混着烂菜叶和下水道的臭气。

    陆川推开窝棚的破木板门，动静很轻。

    屋里，陆小鱼还在睡。

    呼吸声很轻，像只刚出生的小猫。

    陆川摸了摸口袋。

    那里有一块大洋，硬邦邦的。

    这是昨晚“结算”的奖励。

    陆江转身来到巷子口。

    “老张，来五个白面馒头。”

    陆川站在一个馒头铺前，声音沙哑地喊道。

    卖馒头的是个五十多的老头，正拿着一块抹布在擦拭案板。

    听到喊声，老张抬眼看去。

    “是陆川啊！”

    “五个白面馒头，算你四枚铜板好了。”

    老张笑着说道。

    陆川没说话，从兜里掏出几枚铜板，拍在案板上。

    老张利落的包好馒头递了过来。

    陆江拿起白面馒头，转身就回了巷子。

    “这小子，手头怎么大方起来了。”

    老张嘟囔了一句后，继续擦拭着案板。

    要知道陆江可是巷子里除了名的臭苦力。

    就算是贼进他家，都要落泪的那种。

    陆江自己吃了两个白面馒头后，将剩下的三个馒头放在桌子上。

    “哥......”

    陆小鱼的声音怯生生地响起。

    陆川回头，看向刚睡醒的小丫头笑道，“馒头放在桌子上了，一会自己吃。”

    “我先去干活了。”

    说着转身就出了窝棚，直奔码头。

    路过巷口时，没看到那两个青帮的喽啰。

    估计昨晚又是在哪个烟馆通宵过瘾了。

    今天的码头雾气很大。

    陆江到的时候，已经有几十号苦力蹲在地上等活。

    一个个像等着喂食的鹌鹑。

    “都在呢？”

    赵扒皮手里盘着两颗核桃，脸上挂着虚伪的笑走了过来。

    “赵爷早。”

    “赵爷好。”

    ......

    众人稀稀拉拉的应着。

    赵扒皮目光扫过人群，最后落在陆川身上。

    “陆大个子，腿好了？”

    “死不了。”

    陆川淡淡回了一句。

    “嘴还是这么臭。”

    赵扒皮也不恼，指了指旁边的一堆麻袋道，

    “今天这批货是洋人的瓷器，轻，但是易碎。”

    “谁要是碰碎了一个，把命赔上都不够。”

    “这活，工钱翻倍。”

    人群里顿时响起一阵吞咽口水的声音。

    翻倍，那就是六枚铜板。

    够买两斤杂合面了。

    “怎么分？”

    有人问道。

    “老规矩，抢。”

    赵扒皮把茶壶一放，满是玩味地看向众人道，

    “谁抢到算谁的。”

    话音刚落，人群瞬间炸了。

    几十个苦力像疯狗一样冲向那堆麻袋。

    推搡，咒骂，拳脚相加。

    没人讲规矩。

    因为在这种地方，规矩是给死人定的。

    陆川没动。

    他站在原地，看着那群人像沙丁鱼一样挤在一起。

    直到人群散开，每个人都扛着麻袋走远。

    地上还剩最后两包。

    陆川走过去。

    弯腰。

    抓绳。

    起！

    两包麻袋稳稳落在肩头。

    很轻。

    确实比洋面轻多了。

    陆川迈步就要走。

    “慢着。”

    赵扒皮的声音从棚子里传来。

    陆川停下，转头看去。
content_en:
The rain stopped.

    There was still that lingering fishy smell in the air, mixed with the stench of rotten vegetable leaves and sewerage.

    Lu Chuan pushed open the broken wooden door of the shack, and there was very little movement.

    In the room, Lu Xiaoyu was still sleeping.

    The breathing sound is very light, like a newborn kitten.

    Lu Chuan touched his pocket.

    There is a big ocean there, hard.

    This is the reward for last night's "settlement".

    Lu Jiang turned around and came to the entrance of the alley.

    "Lao Zhang, here are five white-flour steamed buns."

    Lu Chuan stood in front of a steamed bun shop and shouted hoarsely.

    The man selling steamed buns was an old man in his fifties, and he was wiping the chopping board with a rag.

    Hearing the shout, Lao Zhang looked up.

    "It's Lu Chuan!"

    "Five white-faced steamed buns will give you four copper coins."

    Lao Zhang said with a smile.

    Lu Chuan didn't say anything. He took out a few coins from his pocket and slapped them on the chopping board.

    Lao Zhang neatly wrapped the steamed buns and handed them over.

    Lu Jiang picked up the white-faced steamed buns, turned around and returned to the alley.

    "This boy, why are you so generous with your money?"

    After Lao Zhang muttered, he continued to wipe the chopping board.

    You must know that Lu Jiang is a notoriously stinky coolie in the alley.

    The kind who would shed tears even if a thief entered his house.

    After Lu Jiang ate two white flour steamed buns himself, he placed the remaining three steamed buns on the table.

    "Brother..."

    Lu Xiaoyu's voice sounded timidly.

    Lu Chuan turned around, looked at the little girl who had just woken up, and smiled, "Put the buns on the table. You can eat them later."

    "I'm going to work first."

    With that said, he turned around and walked out of the shack, heading straight to the dock.

    When passing by the alley, I didn't see the two men from the Qing Gang.

    I guess I stayed up all night in a smoking den last night.

    It's very foggy at the pier today.

    When Lu Jiang arrived, there were already dozens of coolies squatting on the ground waiting for work.

    Each one looks like a quail waiting to be fed.

    "Are you all here?"

    Zhao Bapi walked over with two walnuts in his hand and a false smile on his face.

    "Good morning, Mr. Zhao."

    "Hello, Mr. Zhao."

    ...

    Everyone responded sparsely.

    Zhao Bapi glanced across the crowd, and finally landed on Lu Chuan.

    "Big man Lu, are your legs healed?"

    "Can't die."

    Lu Chuan replied lightly.

    "My mouth still smells so bad."

    Zhao Papi was not annoyed, pointed to the pile of sacks next to him and said,

    "Today's batch of goods is foreign porcelain. It is light but fragile."

    "If anyone breaks one, it won't be enough to pay for it with his life."

    "For this job, the wages will be doubled."

    There was a sudden sound of swallowing in the crowd.

    Double that, and that's six copper coins.

    Enough to buy two kilograms of mixed noodles.

    "How to divide it?"

    someone asked.

    "Old rules, grab."

    Zhao Papi put the teapot down and looked at the crowd with amusement and said,

    "Whoever grabs it gets it."

    As soon as he finished speaking, the crowd exploded.

    Dozens of coolies rushed towards the pile of sacks like mad dogs.

    Pushing, swearing, punches.

    No one follows the rules.

    Because in a place like this, the rules are for the dead.

    Lu Chuan didn't move.

    He stood and watched the group of people packed together like sardines.

    Until the crowd dispersed and everyone walked away carrying the sacks.

    The last two packages were left on the floor.

    Lu Chuan walked over.

    bend over.

    Grab the rope.

    rise!

    Two sacks landed firmly on his shoulders.

    Very light.

    It is indeed much lighter than the ocean surface.

    Lu Chuan took a step to leave.

    "Wait a minute."

    Zhao Papi's voice came from the shed.

    Lu Chuan stopped and turned to look.
